circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: Located on Yas Island in Abu Dhabi, the 5. 281 km Yas Marina Circuit was designed by Hermann Tilke and has served as the venue for Formula One's season-concluding Abu Dhabi Grand Prix since 2009. The track represents the second Middle Eastern Formula One venue to be constructed, following Bahrain's circuit and preceding later additions in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: The Albert Park Circuit is a street track encircling Albert Park Lake in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb, hosting the Formula One Australian Grand Prix each year alongside the Supercars Championship and various supporting events. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 classification status.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Austria, this 4. 326 km circuit served as the venue for the Austrian Grand Prix across two distinct periods: first under its original Österreichring name from 1970 to 1987, then after undergoing reconstruction and shortening as the A1-Ring from 1997 to 2003. The track has undergone significant modifications throughout its history to accommodate modern racing standards.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit, a street track built alongside Baku Boulevard in Azerbaijan, stretches 6. 003 km and ranks as the fourth-longest venue on the Formula One calendar. The circuit debuted in Formula One with the 2016 European Grand Prix, before becoming a permanent fixture the following year under its own Azerbaijan Grand Prix title.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, the Bahrain International Circuit is a 5. 412 km venue that hosted the inaugural Formula One race in the Middle East that year and continues to stage the annual Bahrain Grand Prix alongside various other motorsport events. The FIA Grade 1 facility features multiple track configurations and has previously accommodated Australian V8 Supercars racing and 24-hour endurance competitions.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, Spain, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya is a 4. 657 km all-purpose racing venue featuring a balanced mix of extended straightaways and diverse corner configurations. The track holds FIA Grade 1 certification and accommodates up to 140,700 spectators across its grandstand facilities.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: Spa-Francorchamps is a 7. 004 km Belgian circuit situated near the town of Spa in Wallonia, renowned for hosting the Formula One Belgian Grand Prix since 1950. The track has maintained an unbroken presence on the F1 calendar from 1985 onwards, with only brief absences in 2003 and 2006.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, the Circuit Gilles Villeneuve is a 4. 361-kilometre track that serves as the home of Canada's Formula One Grand Prix. Beyond hosting top-tier single-seater racing, the venue has accommodated various international motorsport championships including sports car racing series and North American touring car competitions.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: Located in Shanghai's Jiading District, the Shanghai International Circuit is a motorsport venue most renowned for hosting the Chinese Grand Prix, which ran annually from 2004 to 2019 before resuming in 2024. The track has expanded its motorsport calendar to include electric racing events alongside the Formula One championship.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Silverstone is an English racing venue situated near Northamptonshire that has served as the traditional home of the British Grand Prix since 1948. The circuit gained particular significance in 1950 when it hosted the inaugural World Championship race, and after alternating with two other tracks for several decades, it became the permanent host of the British Grand Prix from 1987 onward. Beyond Formula One, the track also stages the British leg of the MotoGP championship.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: Located near Budapest in Mogyoród, the Hungaroring is a 4. 381 km circuit that hosted the inaugural Formula One Grand Prix held within the Eastern Bloc in 1986. Built in just eight months, faster than any other F1 venue, the permanent track was constructed outside the city near a major highway after plans for an urban circuit in Budapest's main park were rejected by authorities.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: The Autodromo Nazionale Monza, located near Milan in northern Italy, is a 5. 793 km track constructed in 1922 as Europe's oldest purpose-built racing circuit. Home to the Italian Grand Prix since 1949, the venue has earned its nickname "Temple of Speed" through its distinctive layout featuring extended straights and fast-flowing corners.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka Circuit, situated in Mie Prefecture, Japan, is a 5. 807 km track operated by Honda Mobilityland that serves as a premier venue for Formula One racing and other international motorsport competitions. With a spectator capacity of 155,000, the circuit has established itself as one of the sport's most significant racing destinations.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course that navigates through Paradise, Nevada, running alongside the famous Las Vegas Boulevard with its concentration of major hotels and casinos. The track passes by several iconic Las Vegas landmarks, including MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas as it winds through the urban landscape.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: The Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez is a 4. 304 km circuit in Mexico City, named after two Mexican racing drivers who tragically died in separate incidents during the 1960s. The venue has hosted the Formula One Mexican Grand Prix since 2015 on its current layout, following earlier hosting periods in different configurations that ended in 1992.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary circuit constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, Florida, spanning 3. 363 miles with 19 turns and an average qualifying speed of approximately 139 mph. Designed by specialist circuit architects for the sport, the track joined the Formula One calendar in 2022 as the home of the Miami Grand Prix.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco winds through the streets of Monte Carlo and La Condamine in the Principality of Monaco, covering 3. 337 kilometres around the harbour area. Though officially named the Circuit de Monaco, it is widely known as Monte Carlo since much of the track occupies that particular neighbourhood.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the Dutch coastal dunes near Amsterdam, Circuit Zandvoort is a 4. 259 km track that resumed hosting the Dutch Grand Prix in 2021 after an absence from the Formula One calendar. The venue's partnership with the championship is scheduled to conclude following the 2026 season.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: The Lusail International Circuit is situated north of Doha in Qatar and spans 5. 419 kilometers with a 1. 068-kilometer main straight.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Located in São Paulo, Brazil, Interlagos is a 4. 309 km racing circuit that opened in 1940 and was later renamed in 1985 to commemorate the late Formula 1 driver José Carlos Pace, who perished in an aviation accident. The track operates in a counterclockwise direction and features supporting facilities including a karting venue named after fellow Brazilian racing legend Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street venue in Saudi Arabia positioned along the Red Sea waterfront, serving as the home of the Saudi Arabian Grand Prix since its inaugural Formula One event in 2021.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit winds through Singapore's Downtown Core and Kallang areas, forming a track layout that circles the Marina Bay waterfront.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya spans 4. 657 kilometers and features a balanced mix of extended straights and diverse cornering sequences that test all aspects of driver skill. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 certification and accommodates up to 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: Located in Austin, Texas, the Circuit of the Americas is a 3. 426-mile Grade 1 track that serves as the permanent home of the Formula One United States Grand Prix. The facility also hosts major motorcycle and endurance racing events, including MotoGP and the Lone Star Le Mans, alongside various other motorsport championships.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a Thai-British racing driver currently competing for Williams in Formula One under the Thai flag.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Spanish driver Fernando Alonso currently races for Aston Martin in Formula One, where he has secured two world championships in 2005 and 2006 during his time with Renault, along with 32 Grand Prix victories across 23 seasons. Beyond single-seaters, Alonso has achieved remarkable success in endurance motorsport, including two Le Mans 24 Hours victories with Toyota and the 2018-19 FIA World Endurance Championship, making him the sole driver to have won both a Formula One title and the World Endurance Championship.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli races for Mercedes in Formula One, having secured six Grand Prix victories following his 2025 debut.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British Formula One driver currently competing for the Haas team in the sport's top racing series.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian driver Gabi Bortoleto currently competes in Formula One as a member of the Audi team. The racing talent brings his experience to the sport's top category with the German manufacturer.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Valtteri Bottas, a Finnish competitor, currently races for Cadillac in Formula One after a lengthy career spanning 13 seasons that has yielded ten Grand Prix victories. He previously achieved runner-up finishes in the drivers' championship twice, finishing second to his teammate in both 2019 and 2020 while driving for Mercedes.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Colapinto is an Argentine motorsport competitor who currently drives for Alpine in Formula One.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Jack Doohan, an Australian driver, currently holds a reserve role with Haas in Formula One while competing in European endurance racing for Nielsen Racing in the LMP2 category. He has made seven Grand Prix appearances between 2024 and 2025.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Alpine. The 2020 Italian Grand Prix victory with AlphaTauri remains a significant achievement in his career.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Isack Alexandre Hadjar is a French-Algerian racing driver competing in Formula One for Red Bull Racing under the French banner.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: British driver Lewis Hamilton has established himself as one of motorsport's most decorated competitors, holding multiple Formula One records including the most race victories and pole positions. Currently competing for Ferrari, Hamilton shares the all-time record of seven world championships with Michael Schumacher and has accumulated 207 podium finishes throughout his career.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently races for Audi in Formula One while boasting significant endurance racing credentials, including a 24 Hours of Le Mans victory with Porsche in 2015.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson is a New Zealand-born racing driver currently competing in Formula One with Racing Bulls.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: Monaco-born Charles Leclerc races for Ferrari in Formula One, having secured second place in the 2022 drivers' championship and accumulated nine career victories across his time in the sport.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Danish driver Kevin Magnussen, known as K-Mag, raced in Formula One across two separate periods from 2014-2020 and 2022-2024 before transitioning away from the sport. He now competes as a factory driver for BMW in the FIA World Endurance Championship with WRT and holds a part-time role in NASCAR's Cup Series driving for Trackhouse Racing.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris represents British motorsport in Formula One, driving for McLaren where he secured the 2025 drivers' championship title. The accomplished competitor has claimed 12 Grand Prix victories throughout his eight-season career in the sport.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Haas. Earlier in his career, he claimed victory at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix while driving for Alpine.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Mexican driver Sergio Pérez currently races for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing extensive experience from his 15 seasons in the sport. The 2023 runner-up in the drivers' championship finished that campaign with Red Bull and has secured six race victories throughout his career.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Oscar Piastri, an Australian driver competing for McLaren in Formula One, has secured nine Grand Prix victories during his four-year tenure in the sport.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Daniel Ricciardo, an Australian driver known as "the Honey Badger," competed in Formula One for 14 seasons between 2011 and 2024, securing eight Grand Prix victories during his career.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: British driver George Russell has secured seven race victories during his eight-season Formula One career with Mercedes.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz competes for Williams in Formula One, where he has secured four race victories throughout his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant is an American racing driver who currently competes in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category for Proton Competition. He previously raced in Formula One during 2023 and 2024, and has also competed in IMSA's LMP2 class with Era Motorsport.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian motorsport competitor who currently drives for Aston Martin in Formula One championship racing.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Japanese driver Yuki Tsunoda held a reserve role with Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls during his Formula One tenure spanning 2021 to 2025.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: The Dutch-Belgian driver Max Verstappen has dominated Formula One in recent years, securing four consecutive world championship titles between 2021 and 2024 while racing for Red Bull Racing. Over his 12-season career, he has accumulated 71 Grand Prix victories and continues to compete under the Dutch flag for the same team.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu represents China as a racing driver currently holding a reserve position with Cadillac in Formula One. The Shanghai-born driver competed in the championship between 2022 and 2024, maintaining the unique distinction of being the sole Chinese competitor to have participated in the sport.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: Alpine Racing operates from its Enstone base as Renault's works team following a 2021 rebranding away from the Renault F1 Team name to showcase the sports car marque. The squad competed under French racing colours and powered by Mercedes engines until Renault's factory departure at the conclusion of 2025, with its sole Alpine-era victory coming through Esteban Ocon's triumph at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin has competed in Formula One through different organizational structures over time, with the current racing entity operating as AMR GP Limited under the Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team banner.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari, the racing arm of the Italian luxury automaker Ferrari, holds the distinction of being both the longest-operating and most accomplished team in Formula One history, having participated continuously since the championship's inception in 1950. The squad is colloquially identified by the "Prancing Horse" emblem that adorns their vehicles.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: An American-licensed Formula One team founded by NASCAR owner Gene Haas in 2014, it competed for the first time in the 2016 season. The team is currently led by principal Ayao Komatsu, who assumed the role in 2024 following Guenther Steiner's departure after eight years in charge.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: A Swiss motorsport engineering company established in 1970, Sauber competed in Formula One from 1993 as an independent constructor, achieving notable success in endurance racing including the 1989 Le Mans victory. The team underwent several transformations throughout its three-decade F1 tenure before ceasing operations in 2025, ranking as the fourth-longest-serving constructor by race entries when it departed the sport. Audi acquired the team and its assets in 2024 to establish the foundation for its own F1 programme.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing is a British Formula One outfit headquartered at its state-of-the-art facility in Woking. The team operates as a subsidiary of the broader McLaren Group, which is owned by Bahrain's sovereign wealth fund.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has maintained a presence in Formula One since 1954 as both a constructor and engine supplier, with the current team operating from Brackley under a German licence. The Mercedes-AMG Petronas outfit became jointly owned by Mercedes-Benz, Ineos, and team principal Toto Wolff in January 2022, with equal stakes distributed among the three parties. The marque's racing programme carries the historical "Silver Arrows" designation.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team and constructor that entered the sport in 2024, operating as a second team under the Red Bull GmbH ownership structure alongside Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with a secondary facility in Milton Keynes, the squad functions as a sister outfit to the primary Red Bull team while maintaining its own constructor status.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that debuted in the 2024 season as Red Bull GmbH's second team alongside Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with operations near Milton Keynes, the squad operates as a sister team within the Red Bull organization's two-team structure.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Red Bull Racing, an Austrian-licensed Formula One team headquartered in England, has been a prominent competitor since its establishment in 2005. Part of the Red Bull GmbH conglomerate alongside Racing Bulls, the team was led by Christian Horner for two decades before Laurent Mekies assumed the role in 2025.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering, a British Formula One constructor founded by Frank Williams and Patrick Head in 1977, operates from its Grove, Oxfordshire headquarters. The team will compete as Atlassian Williams F1 Team in 2026, continuing its legacy following Frank Williams's earlier failed racing venture.
